title: The Actor Who Plays Eumaeus in The Odyssey Is Everywhere — Here’s Why You Know Him
summary:
Have you ever watched a movie and thought, “Hey, I know that voice!”? That’s exactly what might happen when you see Christopher Nolan’s new film The Odyssey. One of the actors, John Leguizamo, plays a character named Eumaeus — a loyal friend to the hero Odysseus who also works as a blind swineherd (a person who takes care of pigs). But you’ve probably seen or heard Leguizamo in a hundred other places.

Leguizamo has been acting since the 1980s. His first TV role was on Miami Vice, and his first movie was a dark comedy called Mixed Blood. Since then, he’s been in everything. He voiced Sid the sloth in the Ice Age movies — you know, the funny one who always gets into trouble. He also played Bruno in Encanto, the uncle everyone whispers about. On screen, he’s been a movie star in The Menu, a tough guy in John Wick, and even a lawyer in The Lincoln Lawyer.

But working with Nolan was a new adventure. Nolan is famous for banning phones on set, which surprised Leguizamo. Even more surprising? The director was always right there in the action. “If it’s freezing, he’s freezing. If you’re in a windstorm, he’s in that windstorm,” Leguizamo said. “You never feel alone.” They filmed in Greece and Morocco, and Leguizamo said the pace was intense but felt truly collaborative.

So when you see Eumaeus on screen, remember: that’s the same guy who made you laugh as Sid and gave you chills as Bruno. And now he’s bringing a legendary Greek character to life — with a director who braves the cold right beside him.
why_it_matters: Learning about actors like Leguizamo shows that stars in movies you love often have decades of work behind them, and that even ancient stories can feel fresh when retold by a director who braves the cold with his cast.
